title: new05
live_proof: inspection in the 3.22.0 tree, with a behavioural confirmation: rtreeUpdate -> rtreeDeleteRowid -> nodeRelease/removeNode frees RtreeNode structures that an open read cursor still holds in its RtreeSearchPoint stack, and 3.22.0 has no guard against the nested write. Upstream fixed it in 3.24.0 by counting active cursors and returning SQLITE_LOCKED_VTAB; in the pin the nested DELETE returns SQLITE_OK, and that rc=0 is itself the evidence that this build is the vulnerable one
object: the RtreeNode structures an open read cursor holds in its search-point stack
lifetime_ender: a write to the same R-Tree while the cursor is open frees those nodes, and the free is unconditional: removeNode links the node onto Rtree.pDeleted and does nRef++ rather than freeing it, then rtreeDeleteRowid's reinsertion loop at the end of the function does sqlite3_free(pLeaf) with no reference to nRef at all. Measured 2026-10-16 by probe site 54: nRef_at_free=3 and nRef_at_free=1 on two of the four frees in one run
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator: a read cursor left open across a DELETE on the same rtree, then stepped. The pinned build's SQLITE_OK on the nested write is the liveness check and runs before the defect is reached

status: re-measured on all four readings 2026-10-16 on this platform, and two verdicts change. host ASan is the 2026-10-11 bundle's reading and still applies, because case.c has not changed since 7517a8c2fd5e (2026-10-11) and the amalgamation is the same sha256 7fc92e19: heap-use-after-free, 16 bytes into a 488-byte region, nodeRelease <- rtreeSearchPointPop <- rtreeNext, freed by sqlite3_free <- rtreeDeleteRowid <- rtreeUpdate, allocated by sqlite3_malloc <- nodeAcquire. It could not be re-run: this host currently has no x86 ASan runtime (the Capstone LLVM build has no compiler-rt for the host triple). virtual-malloc faults cause=24 pc=0x3faaa1746c in nodeRelease at fault ADDRESS 0x17, with both controls as declared; virtual-nested-pools faults cause=25 pc=0x3f8561793c in nodeRelease at fault address 0x3f8577dda8, with both controls as declared; cheribsd-revocation faults SIGPROT(34) si_code=2 PROT_CHERI_TAG/untagged-deref pc=0x1d066a = nodeRelease+0x2e, exit 162, with the boot's positive control trapping and revocation knobs 1/0. The case reaches its state in every run (inserted=30, rows=30, nodes=3, nested delete rc=0, so the tree has interior nodes and the pinned build has no SQLITE_LOCKED_VTAB guard). Only the Sublet reading is a detection; see note. The earlier status text said cheribsd-revocation had no verdict, which was a stale 2026-10-04/05 line: the 2026-10-05 and 2026-10-06 runs both record FAULT SIGPROT(34), and the arms block below is right about the signal and wrong about what it means. The arms block is the 2026-10-11 bundle's and is regenerated by derive-verdicts.py when this review ends
note: Re-measured 2026-10-16, and the base and CheriBSD cells are NOT detections. What they fault on is memsys5's in-band freelist metadata, not the stale access. Three conditions coincide in this case and in no other reviewed so far. (1) RtreeNode's first field is RtreeNode *pParent, at offset 0. (2) memsys5 has no block header, so the pointer it returns is the block start and memsys5Link writes Mem5Link{int next; int prev;} over bytes 0..7 -- on both Capstone and CHERI a pointer is a 16-byte capability at offset 0, so those eight integer bytes land on its low half and clear its tag. (3) nodeRelease dereferences exactly that field: if( pNode->pParent ) nodeRelease(pRtree, pNode->pParent). Probe site 54 prints the whole chain on native memsys5 and on CheriBSD purecap alike: FREE p=X nRef_at_free=1 pParent=0x0, then READ p=X nRef_read=1 pParent=0xffffffffffffffff -- memsys5Link's next=-1/prev=-1 terminator -- then RECURSE pParent=0xffffffffffffffff, then the same instruction faulting. On CheriBSD the probe also prints the capability at the stale read: kind=UAF blk=0x223000 tag=1 cb=0x1e5800+262144, i.e. the stale load goes through a fully valid capability bounded to the whole 256 KiB sqlite_heap[] array, and CHERI has nothing to object to; the second witness, kind=CAP-OOB tag=0, is the -1. So on both arms the defective access SUCCEEDS, decrements a refcount in dead memory and drives the branch, and the trap comes two frames later on a pointer the allocator itself manufactured. That is the baseline capability tag check firing, not an allocator-aware mechanism, and it is layout luck: had the block been reissued -- memsys5's own default -- offset 0 would hold a live object's tagged pointer and both arms would be silent, which is exactly what cases 05, 11 and 14 measured. CheriBSD additionally cannot catch this by construction: sqlite_heap[] is a static array, sqlite3_free never calls free(), so there is nothing for revocation to revoke. Sublet is a detection: cause 25 is the lifetime check, it fires at the stale load itself, and its fault address is inside the arena. Also corrected: all three physical rows in results/matrix.tsv are marked, the sublet one included -- it reports cause 24 at pc=0x1021b45e8, which is this same -1 dereference and not the lifetime check, so this review relies on the virtual arm's cause 25. Probe site 54 is new for this case (six hooks: ALLOC, REMOVE, FREE, READ, RECURSE, FREE2) and run-probe-cheri.sh's SITE map now carries [rtreecursor]=54
fault_sites_why: rtreeNext -> rtreeSearchPointPop -> nodeRelease reads pNode->nRef out of the freed block (PROVENANCE.md, host ASan: READ of size 4 into a 488-byte region). Declared 2026-10-10 after the virtual runs resolved faults there; the reason is the source and PROVENANCE.md cited, which predate those runs. INSUFFICIENT AS AN ATTRIBUTION, measured 2026-10-16: nodeRelease recurses into pNode->pParent, so the defective access and the consequence of letting it succeed are the SAME FUNCTION, the same pc offset (+144 in both virtual images) and the same instruction (lw at offset 24 from the node, nRef under the 16-byte-pointer layout). All three arms fault there and they are not reporting the same event. The discriminator is the fault ADDRESS: 0x17 on base Capstone, which is (-1) + 24 and can only be the recursive call on a pParent that memsys5 overwrote, against 0x3f8577dda8 on Sublet, which is inside the arena and is the node itself. A function-level attribution, and here even a pc-level one, cannot separate them; see note and PROVENANCE.md.
